**Outputs:** Fourier Transform value $\hat{u}_\mathcal{T}(\boldsymbol{\xi})$; Gradient of the transform with respect to vertex positions $\frac{\partial \hat{u}_\mathcal{T}}{\partial \mathbf{v}_p}$.

**Index Permutation:** Set $\mathbf{v}_4 = \mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_0 = \mathbf{v}_3$.
For $p \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, define indices $p^- = p-1$ and $p^+ = p+1$.
**Edge Computation:** Compute edge vectors opposite to vertex $p$: $\mathbf{e}_p = \mathbf{v}_{p^-} - \mathbf{v}_{p^+}$.
Compute edge lengths $l_p = \|\mathbf{e}_p\|$.
**Normal and Area:** Compute the unnormalized area vector $\mathbf{A}_{vec} = \mathbf{e}_3 \times \mathbf{e}_1$.
The area is $A_\mathcal{T} = \|\mathbf{A}_{vec}\| / 2$.
The unit normal is $\mathbf{N}_\mathcal{T} = \mathbf{A}_{vec} / (2 A_\mathcal{T})$.
**Outward Normals:** For each $p$, compute the non-normalized outward normal to the triangle on edge $\mathbf{e}_p$: $\mathbf{w}_p = \mathbf{e}_p \times \mathbf{N}_\mathcal{T}$.
**Gradient of Area:** The gradient of the triangle area with respect to vertex $\mathbf{v}_p$ is $\frac{\partial A_\mathcal{T}}{\partial \mathbf{v}_p} = -\frac{\mathbf{w}_p}{2}$.
